survivors_flagged.one_line: The Second Circuit reversed the $16B YPF judgment on 2026-03-27 and the stock fell about 50%. A Supreme Court cert petition was filed 2026-09-30, with a conference decision likely Dec-Jan. Cert is unlikely to be granted, but a grant would re-rate a crushed stock, so the payoff is lopsided. The treaty-arbitration route is a second option.

FDA decision on the deramiocel BLA is due 2026-11-22, pushed back from August by a major amendment that added 24-month open-label data. Only one source reports the new date, so confirm it in Capricor's filings. The FDA panel voted 9-3 against efficacy on 07-29 and the stock plunged. An approval would be a large upside surprise, but the decision is about 3 weeks out, so the setup is late-arc.

Staged IPO lockup ends fully around Nov 9-mid Nov 2026 (or 2 trading days after Q3 results). Stock is about 20% below the $185 IPO price after insider Form 144 filings, so this is a buy-after-the-overhang-clears setup. Dates conflict between sources.

$750M of 7% unsecured notes mature Jun 2027. A secured refi (around 9.5%, ring-fencing IRU obligations) was guided for Q3 and is still not confirmed. Stock is down 85% to about $6.3 and Q3 earnings land next week. The refi/LME outcome is a real binary, but it is already deep in the price.

verified.catalyst: The Supreme Court decides whether to hear the Petersen/Eton Park v. Argentina (YPF) case. Granting review would revive a claim the market has written off since the Second Circuit reversed the roughly $16B judgment on 2026-03-27.
verified.dated_milestone: Cert petition reportedly filed 2026-09-30 (I could not check this). Argentina's opposition brief and conference distribution are next, with a decision likely Dec-2026 to Jan-2027. Nearer date: 3Q26 results on 2026-11-04.
verified.instrument: BUR common (NYSE, $3.65; also listed in London). Long-dated calls would express the lopsided payoff better than shares if liquidity allows.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 is met: the counterparty is named (Republic of Argentina / YPF). G2 is not met: there is no commitment, only a discretionary court decision. G3 is partial: the stock implies close to zero value for the YPF claim, but I could not re-derive the current carrying value of the YPF asset or the slice of the claim that belongs to Burford.
verified.edge: L-M. The event is real and dated, but the Supreme Court grants roughly 1-5% of paid petitions, and even a grant only reopens the case; it does not reinstate the award. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about 0% to slightly negative. The London price was 286p (about $3.85) on 2026-09-24, just before the filing, against $3.65 today, so none of the cert option is priced. Remaining capture if cert is granted: an estimated +40-90%, toward $5-7. The 200-day average is $5.38 and the pre-reversal 52-week high was $10.10. A grant would restore part of that, not all of it. Probability-weighted, the expected value is small. The asymmetry is real, but the odds are weak.
verified.primary_source: Proactive Investors via FMP news, 2026-03-30 (Second Circuit reversal, 40%+ drop). Burford press releases via FMP: senior secured notes, 2026-09-14; jury verdict statement, 2026-09-28; 3Q26 results date, 2026-10-26. FMP quote, 2026-11-02 ($3.65, 52-week range 2.86-10.10). Cert petition filing date taken from the triage flag and not independently verified.
verified.analysis: FMP news confirms the Second Circuit reversal on 2026-03-27 (Proactive Investors, 2026-03-30: shares fell more than 40%) and the stock's collapse since: $3.65 now against a $10.10 52-week high, with a 2026-09-14 issue of $300M of 8% senior secured notes. I could not independently confirm the 2026-09-30 cert petition or a conference date because the web-search budget was exhausted, and I did not reach the 10-Q for the YPF carrying value or the debt stack ahead of the common. Treat the numerator as unverified. That alone caps the score at 4 under the provenance rule. This is a low-probability, discretionary court binary, not a commitment. A further possible source of upside is the 2026-09-25 jury verdict of $5.7B in a patent case in which Burford has a financial interest; Burford's share of it is not disclosed. That is a separate, undated thesis. Keep on WATCH. Re-score if cert is granted, if the Solicitor General is invited to give a view (CVSG), or after the 3Q26 numbers show the YPF write-down and how the capital structure stands.

verified.catalyst: The FDA must act on Capricor's deramiocel BLA for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by 2026-11-22. The date was extended after a major amendment added 24-month HOPE-3 open-label extension data, and the 07-29 advisory panel voted 9-3 against efficacy.
verified.dated_milestone: PDUFA target action date 2026-11-22 (approval or CRL). After that, the securities class action covering the 12/17/2025-7/26/2026 class period moves to the lead-plaintiff stage, and the Q3 10-Q is due in mid-November.
verified.instrument: CAPR common (NASDAQ), $6.93-6.95 on 2026-11-02, market cap about $401M, about 58M shares. The risk is binary, so the position should be small. Defined-risk call spreads would also work if the options are liquid.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 passes: the counterparty is named (FDA/CBER acting on the deramiocel BLA). G2 passes: there is a concrete, dated PDUFA goal of 2026-11-22, confirmed in the company's own press release. G3 passes only partly: an approval is not priced in (about $6.95 now vs about $19.7 before the panel), but the market's discount reflects real negative panel evidence, so the gap is not a clean mispricing.
verified.edge: L-M. The date is confirmed and the event is forward-looking, but the discount looks fair rather than mispriced. Run-up: +74% from the post-panel base of about $4.00 (07-30 to 08-13 closes $3.85-4.21) to $6.95. Most of that came on 08-14, when the major amendment and PDUFA extension became public (+58% that day, 66M shares traded). Remaining: about +160% to a favorable-resolution value of about $18. I took that value from the pre-panel close of $19.70, haircut for a likely narrow label and launch ramp. On a CRL the price would fall to roughly $3.0-3.5, about cash per share, a 50-55% drop. At 25% approval odds (low after a 9-3 negative panel and the allegations about the analysis plan), the expected value is about 0.25*18 + 0.75*3.3 = $7.0, roughly today's price. The event has been partly harvested, the large residual reflects real binary risk, and I see no informational edge.
verified.primary_source: Capricor press release (GlobeNewswire, 2026-10-05) 'Positive HOPE-3 Open-Label Extension Data on Upper Limb Function in DMD at 2026 World Muscle Society Congress', which states that the data are in the BLA major amendment and gives a PDUFA target action date of November 22, 2026. Capricor Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet (filed 2026-08-14). FMP EOD prices for 2026-07-20 to 2026-11-02.
verified.analysis: Capricor's own 2026-10-05 GlobeNewswire release confirms the PDUFA date of November 22, 2026, so the single-source date concern is resolved. The capital structure is clean: about $238M in cash and investments at 6/30/26 (10-Q filed 2026-08-14), no preferred stock and no funded debt, only about $91M of lease liabilities. Cash is therefore a real floor of about $3-4 per share after Q3 burn, and nothing in the waterfall eats into the upside. The setup is late-arc and roughly fairly priced. The 9-3 panel vote against efficacy, plus class-action allegations that the HOPE-3 statistical analysis plan was rewritten one day before unblinding without FDA agreement, keep approval odds near 20-30%. That makes the probability-weighted value of about $7 close to the $6.95 price, so this stays a WATCH binary at score 5 and does not qualify as ACTIVE. Gap: my web-search budget was used up before I could look for any FDA label-negotiation or late-cycle meeting disclosures in recent filings, so I could not check for them.
